comment:
Make it read the way the real castle does, in this order of importance:
1. VERTICALITY. It reads wide and squat; it must read tall and narrow. Make the stair turret (the slender round tower beside the Palas) the unmistakable high point: thinner, with an octagonal belfry stage near the top and a needle spire, clearly 15+ blocks above every other roof. Make the Palas taller and narrower-looking (5 storeys, steeper roof, a higher ridge), and put the whole castle on a much taller sheer cliff: deepen the rock crag so it drops away steeply on the front and sides (extend the build downward for this, don't squash the castle to fit).
2. PALAS FACADES. Replace the flat grid of dark rectangles with Romanesque-revival windows: paired and triple round-arched windows with thin white column mullions, grouped in vertical bays between pilaster strips, each storey's windows different from the next. Give the courtyard-facing front a two-storey open arcaded balcony (the Singers' Hall loggia), and make the north-face balcony bold and visible.
3. ROOFS AND CAPS. Gold finials on every spire and cone; vary the slate a little between the big roofs and the turret caps so they aren't one flat black; keep the cones slender and pointed.
4. INTERIORS (last, as time allows). Inside the Palas: the Throne Hall, two storeys tall, blue walls with gold, an apse at one end with a raised gold throne platform and a large chandelier; above it the Singers' Hall, a long hall with a coffered wooden ceiling and the loggia doors. Give the other storeys floors so windows look into rooms.
Keep everything else as it is: the gatehouse, the gate towers, the courtyards, the Knights' House and Bower, the palette.
summary: Castle lifted onto a ~26-block steep crag (grid now 112x118x52 vs the ~75 asked). Stair turret is thin with an octagonal belfry and needle spire to y98, ridge y74. Palas is 5 storeys with Romanesque bay windows, loggia, bold balcony and interiors. Gold finials on all cones/spires/gables; slate varied; check shows 0 floating blocks.
applied: VERTICALITY: the whole castle is built at its own levels then lifted 16 blocks onto a deepened crag (terraces at y26/32, falloff ~4.4 blocks per block, brick retaining wall only on the top rows) so the cliff drops steeply on the front and sides without squashing the castle.

VERTICALITY: the stair turret is now r2 (was r3) to y66, with a corbel, an octagonal belfry with arched openings (y67-73) and a needle spire. Its tip is y98 against the Palas ridge at y74 and corner-turret caps at about 73, so it is about 24 blocks above every other roof.
VERTICALITY: the Palas is 5 storeys (wall top y52, was y44) with a very-steep roof (ridge y74, was y59). The corner and wing turrets are raised to clear the new wall height.

PALAS FACADES: pilaster strips divide every face into bays. Each storey has its own round-arched group with white quartz-pillar mullions: single, pair, triple (tall centre with two lancets), pair, then lancets. The wing's north gable gets the same treatment.

PALAS FACADES: two-storey open arcaded loggia on the north front (x90-102, y38-50) over a rusticated stone base, with doors and windows into the hall behind. The north balcony is now 5 deep and 10 wide, on corbels and quartz piers rising from the lower court, with French doors, gold-capped posts, lanterns and lozenge banners.

ROOFS AND CAPS: gold block plus rod finial on every turret cap, gate-tower cap and the stair spire. The main tower, bower and gable ends also got gold finials. Turret caps use the lighter 'slate' palette against the Palas's dark-slate. Cones stay slender. I removed the stray dormers on the tower caps, which were orphan blocks.

INTERIORS: floors on every Palas storey (y23, 37, 44). The Throne Hall is two storeys tall with blue concrete walls and gold bands, a raised gold throne platform, a gold-framed throne and three chandeliers. The Singers' Hall has a coffered spruce and dark-oak ceiling with hanging lanterns.
skipped: The Throne Hall apse is a flat gold-and-blue niche, not a curved apse: the exterior wall is straight and a curve didn't fit in the time.

The Singers' Hall sits in the Palas's north half, behind the loggia, rather than above the Throne Hall (its own storey, y38-43). The two halls are in different halves of the Palas, so the Throne Hall doesn't sit under it.
Height is 118 blocks against the ~75 asked, because the build had to extend downward and the stair turret and Palas needed to grow. Nothing was squashed to fit.
The slate variation is subtle: the lighter 'slate' palette on the caps reads only slightly lighter than the Palas's dark-slate.
A few preexisting orphan blocks and tree leaves remain in the final check (48 orphans, 0 floating). `mcd check` and `mcd palette` need `node --stack-size=60000` on this build.
